events.title: The birth of Karol Wojtyła
events.shortBlurb: The future Pope John Paul II was born in the Polish town of Wadowice…
body: On 18 May 1920 Karol Józef Wojtyła was born at Wadowice in southern Poland, the second son of a retired infantry officer. He lost his mother Emilia in 1929, his elder brother Edmund, a physician, to scarlet fever in 1932, and his father in 1941, and was left alone before his twenty-first year.

Under the German occupation he labored in a quarry and then in the Solvay chemical works, studying secretly in the clandestine seminary of Kraków kept by Cardinal Adam Sapieha. He was ordained a priest on 1 November 1946, became Archbishop of Kraków in 1964, and was made a cardinal in 1967.

On 16 October 1978 the conclave elected him pope, the first non-Italian in 455 years, and he took the name John Paul II. His pontificate of nearly twenty-seven years ended with his death on 2 April 2005; he was canonized by Pope Francis on 27 April 2014, together with Pope John XXIII.

sources.text: Vatican biography of Pope St. John Paul II (vatican.va)
